newsitem.title: USA: Merrill Lynch mulls its own index funds - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch mulls its own index funds - WSJ.

text.p: Merrill Lynch & Co Inc is considering offering its own stock-index funds to investors, the Wall Street Journal reported Monday.

Quoting anonymous sources, the Journal said the brokerage's asset-management subsidiary, Merrill Lynch Asset Management, is pondering the launch of several index funds to its "wrap-account" customers in 1997.
Wrap accounts lump fees together into one annual payment, typically one percent to three percent of the total assets managed.

The article said Merrill Lynch would only confirm that it plans to offer to small-investor clientele a domestic stock-index fund, an international stock-index fund and a bond-index fund sometime in 1997.
